english: Let $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ be defined by $f(x)=\max\left\{\{x\},\dfrac{|x|}{4}\right\}$, where $\{t\}=t-[t]$ and $[t]$ denotes the greatest integer less than or equal to $t$. Then the sum of all the points of the interval $(-4,4)$ at which $f$ is not differentiable is ______.
hindi: माना कि $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$, $f(x)=\max\left\{\{x\},\dfrac{|x|}{4}\right\}$ द्वारा परिभाषित है, जहाँ $\{t\}=t-[t]$ है तथा $[t]$, $t$ से कम या उसके बराबर महत्तम पूर्णांक को दर्शाता है। तब अन्तराल $(-4,4)$ के उन सभी बिन्दुओं का योग, जिन पर $f$ अवकलनीय नहीं है, ______ है।
solution: $x\ge0$: $x-n>\frac{x}{4}\iff x>\frac{4n}{3}$, which lies in $[n,n+1)$ for $n=0,1,2$: corners at $\frac{4}{3},\frac{8}{3}$ ($n=0$ gives $x>0$, no corner)
$x<0$: $x-n>-\frac{x}{4}\iff x>\frac{4n}{5}$, in $[n,n+1)$ for $n=-4,\dots,-1$: corners at $-\frac{16}{5},-\frac{12}{5},-\frac{8}{5},-\frac{4}{5}$ (slopes $1$ and $-\frac14$ differ)
Integers $n=-3,\dots,3$: as $x\to n^{-}$, $\{x\}\to1>\frac{|n|}{4}$, so $f\to1$, but $f(n)=\frac{|n|}{4}<1$: discontinuous, hence not differentiable
solution_full: Integer points $n\in\{-3,\dots,3\}$: $\lim_{x\to n^{-}}u(x)=1$ while $v(n)=\frac{|n|}{4}\le\frac34<1$, so $\lim_{x\to n^{-}}f(x)=1$. But $f(n)=\max\left\{0,\frac{|n|}{4}\right\}=\frac{|n|}{4}\neq1$. So $f$ is discontinuous, and hence not differentiable, at each of these $7$ integers (including $0$).
Non-integer points: $f$ is the maximum of two functions that are differentiable away from integers and $0$; $f$ fails to be differentiable only where $u=v$ with different slopes.

For $x\in(n,n+1)$ with $n\ge0$: $u=x-n$ (slope $1$), $v=\frac{x}{4}$ (slope $\frac14$). $u=v\iff x=\frac{4n}{3}$. This lies in $(n,n+1)$ iff $0<\frac{n}{3}<1$, i.e. $n=1,2$: $x=\frac43,\frac83$. (For $n=3$, $x=4$ is outside $(3,4)$.)

For $x\in(n,n+1)$ with $n\le-1$: $u=x-n$ (slope $1$), $v=-\frac{x}{4}$ (slope $-\frac14$). $u=v\iff x=\frac{4n}{5}$, which lies in $(n,n+1)$ iff $-\frac{n}{5}<1$, true for $n=-4,-3,-2,-1$: $x=-\frac{16}{5},-\frac{12}{5},-\frac{8}{5},-\frac{4}{5}$.
At each such crossing the slopes differ, so there is a corner.
originality_note: New: the maximum of the sawtooth {x} and the tent |x|/4 is asymmetric, because {x} rises on both sides of 0 while |x|/4 changes slope, so the crossings are at 4n/3 for x > 0 and at 4n/5 for x < 0, and every integer except +-4 is a jump (way 2: a function built as a max of two simple functions). Closest known: min{{x}, {-x}} or max of [x]-type and linear functions. Different because: the two sides need different crossing formulas and the sum is asked, so missing one class changes the answer.
key_step: Split into unit intervals; crossings x = 4n/3 (x > 0) and 4n/5 (x < 0) give corners, and every integer in (-4,4) is a jump of the max.
justification: Three ideas combined with interval-by-interval casework and no options: jumps of the max at integers, corners at crossings, and asymmetric crossing formulas on the two sides. Similar counting demand to 2023-P2-Q6 (L3), below 2026-P1-Q10 (L4) which has more cancellation.

concept_use.Continuity and Differentiability of func: One-sided limits at integers show discontinuity (hence non-differentiability); unequal one-sided slopes at crossings give corners.
{x} = x - n on [n, n+1) and its jump from 1 to 0 at each integer drive both the crossings and the discontinuities.
f = max{{x}, |x|/4} switches branch at the crossings {x} = |x|/4, where the max has a corner.

stem_review: Read as a student: f has domain and codomain, {t} and [t] are defined, the interval is open so +-4 are excluded, 'sum of all the points' has one reading. Checked by a fine grid scan that the 13 points are exactly those listed. Answer -4, a negative integer. Changed: reworded the ending to 'the sum of all the points ... is'.
